# CHAKRAVYUH — video brief

**For:** generating a short demo video of what this system actually is.
**Source of every number below:** the artefacts in this repository, regenerated by
`make artefacts` in about 35 seconds. Nothing here is estimated, rounded for effect, or aspirational.

**Project:** CHAKRAVYUH — policy fuzzing for emergency telecommunications governance
**Team:** Quantum QAI · Ranny Nayyar
**Event:** ITU AI for Good Sandbox Build-a-thon 5.0, New Delhi, 10 October 2026
**Licence:** Apache-2.0

**Target length:** 2 min 30 s – 3 min. Eight scenes.
**Tone:** an engineer showing their instrument, not a product launch. Calm, specific, unhurried.
Let the numbers carry the weight. No triumphal music over a statistic.

---

## The one-sentence version

> CHAKRAVYUH replays a real cyclone under three countries' telecom laws and reports, with clause
> citations, which legal obligations fail to fire in time — before the next cyclone does.

## The three things the video must land

1. **ITU-T Y.3172 nodes are named in the code, not on a slide.** A decorator registers each entry
   point; the conformance map is generated by walking that registry. Delete a function and the map
   loses it.
2. **Provenance is enforced, not asserted.** Sources pinned by SHA-256, clause text stored
   verbatim with page numbers and document-level links, and a *computed* confidence rating that
   refuses to say "certain" when the underlying text is still a summary.
3. **The evaluation is measured and the limits are stated out loud.** Including the ones that make
   the project look weaker.

## Scene 1 · The problem  (0:00 – 0:20)

**On screen.** A cyclone track over the Bay of Bengal, 16–20 May 2020. Nine real districts light
up across Odisha and West Bengal, then one across the border: BD-KHULNA.

**Narration.**
> When a cyclone makes landfall, whether the warning reaches you is not only an engineering
> question. It is a legal one. Somebody must have the power to issue it, in your language, before
> the storm arrives — and if no clause grants that power, the warning does not go out.
>
> You find that out during the cyclone. We wanted to find it out before.

**Note for the animator.** Amphan was real. The IMD timeline, the warned districts, the landfall
time and the network-capacity figures are from the public record. Do not dramatise casualties —
this project makes no claim about human outcomes and the video must not either.

---

## Scene 2 · What it is  (0:20 – 0:50)

**On screen.** Three layers, built one at a time:

```
PROPOSE   six role-bound agents        Y.3172 node M
DECIDE    one deterministic Game Master Y.3172 node D
PROVE     a hash-chained ledger         Y.3172 node SINK
```

**Narration.**
> Six agents play the institutions: the Home Department, the State Disaster Management Authority,
> a telecom operator's network centre, CERT-In, the authority on the other side of the border, and
> a legal adviser. Each sees only its own inbox — delayed, redacted, incomplete — and each proposes
> actions it believes the law allows.
>
> Nothing they propose happens on their say-so. Every proposal is resolved by one deterministic
> engine against one rulebook, in one fixed order. Agents reason. Rules decide. The ledger records
> both.

**The line to hold on screen.**
> **Agents propose. Deterministic code decides.**

**Note.** This is DeepMind's Concordia pattern with one deliberate change: the Game Master is
ordinary Python, not a model. That is what makes a run reproducible. No LangGraph, no AutoGen, no
CrewAI — the orchestration is hand-written, because a framework's scheduler between the proposal
and the verdict would cost the determinism claim.

---

## Scene 3 · The result  (0:50 – 1:20)

**On screen.** The scorecard. Four safety properties down the side, three legal regimes across the
top. Fill the cells one row at a time.

| | **India** | **Bangladesh** | **United States** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1** relief traffic survives a suspension | **FAIL** −60 pp | PASS +40 | PASS +40 |
| **P2** no forged order causes an irreversible act | **FAIL** −1 exec | PASS 0 | PASS 0 |
| **P3** every area alerted in time, in a local language | **FAIL** −7140 min | PASS +345 | PASS +345 |
| **P4** disaster roaming active within the deadline | **FAIL** −855 min | **FAIL** −855 | PASS +345 |

**Narration.**
> Same cyclone. Same districts. Same agents. Same random seed. The only thing that changed between
> these three columns is the rulebook.
>
> Under current Indian law, all four properties fail — and for each one, at least one comparator
> regime passes on identical input. That difference is the finding. And because the engine records
> which rule it applied, the finding is attributable to specific clauses.

**Note.** Margins are not all the same unit, and the UI says so rather than flattening them:
percentage points for P1, executions for P2, minutes of slack for P3 and P4.

## Scene 4 · Y.3172, in the code  (1:20 – 1:45)

**This is theme 1. Do not skip it.**

**On screen.** A line of real Python, then the generated map beside it.

```python
@node("P")
def evaluate(proposal, pack, view) -> Verdict:
    ...
```

Then the counts, appearing as a bar per node:

| Node | Registered entry points | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| SRC | 8 | acts, rules, registers, scenario definitions |
| C | 6 | ingest of source documents into the knowledge base |
| PP | 8 | clause structuring, policy-pack compilation |
| M | 15 | agents that propose actions |
| P | 2 | deterministic legality decision |
| D | 10 | message bus, event release, Game Master resolution |
| SINK | 23 | ledger, failure atlas, gap register, UI |
| | **72 total** | |

**Narration.**
> Conformance claims are easy to put on a slide. Here, every entry point in the system declares
> its ITU-T Y.3172 node with a decorator, and the conformance map is generated by walking that
> registry at build time. Seventy-two registrations across seven nodes.
>
> Delete a function, and it disappears from the map. A test fails if the map and the code disagree.
> The mapping cannot drift, because nobody maintains it by hand.

**Say also, briefly:** Y.3173 governs the human-in-the-loop gate; X.1303 and OASIS CAP 1.2 govern
the alert envelopes; E.106 is the obligation P1 measures.

## Scene 5 · Provenance  (1:45 – 2:15)

**This is theme 2. It is the heart of the project.**

**On screen, part A — a source pinned by hash.** A row from the manifest:

```
held   IN-SUSP-2024   Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules, 2024
       G.S.R. 724(E), Gazette Extraordinary No. 665, 22 Nov 2024
       sha256 f60ca6db4d91b116…   6 pages   5/5 required strings present
```

**On screen, part B — a clause quoted verbatim, with its page and its document.**

> **IN.TA2023.s20.2** · Telecommunications Act, 2023 (Act 44 of 2023) · s.20(2) · **page 9**
>
> *"On the occurrence of any public emergency or in the interest of public safety, the Central
> Government or a State Government … may … direct that any telecommunication service or class of
> telecommunication services … shall be suspended."*
>
> clause sha256 `be54689ffe2ccd79…` · source PDF sha256 `302df7ba4ed69e90…`
> `egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/250880.pdf`

**Narration.**
> Every claim this system makes about the law points at text we hold. Each source document is
> pinned by SHA-256 and checked against strings only the real instrument contains. Each clause is
> stored with the instrument's own words, the page it sits on, a hash of that text, and a link to
> the document it came from.
>
> A hash proves a file did not change. It does not prove the file is complete — so each source also
> declares what it must contain.

**On screen, part C — the near-miss.** Red panel, held long enough to read:

> The only obtainable copy of the Telecom Cyber Security Rules 2024 is a **composite**: six pages
> of one instrument, three pages of a different one, and most of the rules missing. Searching it
> for "authenticate" returns zero hits — which would have *confirmed* a finding that no
> authentication requirement exists.
>
> The completeness check caught it. The source is marked **partial**, and the finding it feeds is
> capped.

**Narration over part C.**
> This is the failure the project exists to prevent: an absence of evidence read as evidence of
> absence. A document that downloads with HTTP 200 is not the same as the right document.

## Scene 6 · Measured, and honest  (2:15 – 2:45)

**This is theme 3. Show the weaknesses on screen, not only in the voiceover.**

**On screen, part A — what was measured.**

| Retrieval mode | recall@5 | MRR | abstention separability |
|---|---|---|---|
| BM25 | 0.979 | 0.907 | 0.921 |
| vector | 0.979 | 0.894 | 0.921 |
| **hybrid (BM25 + vector, RRF)** | **0.979** | **0.908** | **0.956** |
| tree | 0.312 | 0.299 | 0.792 |

48 answerable questions with gold clause ids, plus 5 whose honest answer is that the knowledge base
cannot say. Adviser: **23/23** never cited a clause outside the retrieved set; **19/23** named the
correct clause.

**On screen, part B — the search that finds the failures.**

> **612 mutated worlds.** Hypothesis property-based fuzzing escalates damage, delays channels and
> forges orders, then shrinks each violation to the smallest mutation sequence that still breaks it.
> Two minimal counterexamples survived shrinking — each one mutation long, each naming the clauses
> in force when it broke.
>
> Under the India pack, the fuzzer ran **zero** mutations. All four properties already fail on the
> unmutated scenario. There was nothing left to fuzz, and the report says so rather than quietly
> reporting a search that never happened.

**On screen, part C — the limits. Hold these.**

> - **0 of 11** registered gaps are rated `certain`. Every one reads `likely`.
> - **47 of 157** clause records are still model-written or secondary summaries, not the
>   instrument's own words.
> - **Three primary documents are missing** — the complete TCS Rules 2024, the 2025 amendment
>   (G.S.R. 771(E)), and DoT SOP-2020. Each one caps a specific finding, and the register names which.
> - **0 of 23** adviser cases have been checked by a human. The score is mechanical.
> - **2 of 22** rubric checks are **waived**, with the reason written in the check's own code.
> - It is a simulation. No money, no casualties, no confidence intervals. A margin is a distance
>   from a threshold inside this model, not a prediction about the world.

**Narration.**
> Confidence is computed, never asserted. A finding is allowed to read "certain" only when every
> clause it cites carries the instrument's own words. Right now, none of them do — so none of them
> says certain.
>
> That rating will rise on its own as the missing documents are obtained. No row needs rewriting
> for that to happen. The system is built to be honest about what it does not yet know.

## Scene 7 · Proof  (2:45 – 3:00)

**On screen.** Three ledgers, then the chain breaking.

```
amphan_2020__bangladesh__rule__seed0      7,996 entries   head ebfded95d0a7347a   chain intact
amphan_2020__fcc_mdri__rule__seed0        4,198 entries   head c30e57aca8ed6906   chain intact
amphan_2020__india_current__rule__seed0     928 entries   head 7292efb8de09e93a   chain intact

…one field edited in a sealed copy…

amphan_2020__india_current__rule__seed0.tampered   payload tampered at seq 45: hash mismatch
amphan_2020__bangladesh__rule__seed0.tampered      payload tampered at seq 72: hash mismatch
```

**Narration.**
> Every event, proposal, verdict, effect and property check is appended to a chain where each
> entry commits to the one before it. Change a single byte and verification names the exact
> sequence number where the chain breaks.
>
> And it is reproducible: the same seed replays to the same head hash, which a test asserts.

## Details worth a shot of their own, if there is room

- **CAP alerts are real envelopes, and region-aware.** Odisha districts receive `or-IN` (Odia),
  West Bengal `bn-IN` (Bengali, India) — and under the Bangladesh pack, BD-KHULNA receives
  `bn-BD`. Same language, different region, because a CAP envelope crossing a border is not the
  same envelope. Sent timestamps use the scenario clock, not wall clock:
  `2020-05-16T09:00:00+05:30`.
- **A refusal is recorded, never filtered.** When India's SDMA proposes alerting across the border,
  the engine answers:
  `BLOCK — prohibited_by_rule: IN.R.NO_CROSS_BORDER_ALERT (Domestic alerting authority holds no
  power to alert across an international border)`. An overreach that is silently filtered out is a
  finding destroyed; one that is blocked is a finding recorded.
- **The human gate reports on itself.** One irreversible suspension was held under Y.3173 and
  released by the batch timer. The run reports the approver as `auto_batch` — it does not claim a
  person reviewed it.
- **The adversarial test is labelled.** The forged order (`sim03`, T+5715, claiming to be the Home
  Department, Government of West Bengal) is marked `synthetic: true` and `authentic: false` in the
  ledger. It is a constructed test, not a historical event, and the data says so.

## Things the video must not say

These are not stylistic preferences. The repository's own NOTICE and tests forbid them.

- ❌ "ITU-certified", "ITU-approved", "ITU-compliant", "endorsed by the ITU".
  ✅ **"aligned with and mapped to"** ITU-T recommendations. That is the exact wording in NOTICE,
  and a test fails the build if any file claims otherwise.
- ❌ Any accuracy percentage, confidence interval, or statistical claim about real-world outcomes.
  A margin is a distance from a threshold inside the model.
- ❌ "Proves that Indian law is unsafe." It reports that, in this model, under this scenario, with
  this seed, four properties fail where comparator regimes pass. Say that.
- ❌ Casualty, damage or cost figures. The system produces none.
- ❌ "AI decides" / "the AI recommends suspending the network." No model decides anything, and a
  test walks the import graph to keep it that way.

## Where the AI is, if asked

Three places, and only one is a language model:

- **Agent reasoning** — three interchangeable tiers behind one protocol: deterministic rule twins,
  an LLM tier through a record/replay cache, and an optional external tier. The demo runs the rule
  twins, so it needs no credential and no network.
- **Retrieval** — BM25 plus vector embeddings, fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion, over 157 clause
  records.
- **Search** — Hypothesis property-based fuzzing. This is the component that actually finds the
  failures.

The policy engine has no model in its transitive import graph, and
`tests/test_p10_repo_standard.py` fails the build if one ever appears.
